requirements.statement: Custody treats framework and housekeeping files as not shipped code: .claude/** except .claude/rules/**, CLAUDE.md, .gitattributes, .gitignore. .claude/rules/** and application source stay shipped. (Must pass: no)
requirements.source: TRD Objectives table O1; investigation O1 (issue #153). No PRD file exists under docs/PRD for this feature; the investigation is the TRD's named source.

requirements.statement: When a merge-up changes a shipped-class file that no covers record names, custody puts in doubt only the criteria whose covers share that file's directory. A file nothing can be related to still widens to every must-pass criterion. (Must pass: YES)
requirements.source: TRD Objectives table O2; investigation O2 (issue #153)

requirements.statement: Before re-proving, custody states what changed since the anchor and the scope chosen (none, targeted or full) with the reason; the gate contracts say so. (Must pass: no)
requirements.source: TRD Objectives table O3; investigation O3 (issue #153)

requirements.statement: Design criteria (ST-<board id> rows proved by verify-design-structure, DC-<frame stem> rows proved by verify-design-comparison) get covers built from docs/ui/<slug>/design-map.json: board route, the page file serving that route, and the files of the components the board names. A board that cannot be fully resolved stays without covers and is reported, never guessed. (Must pass: YES)
requirements.source: TRD Objectives table O4; investigation O4 (issue #154, owner decision 2026-11-16)

requirements.statement: The verification regression pass re-checks a criterion that has no covers record only when a changed file relates to it, not on any Debug edit; the report says how many criteria were re-checked and why, per reason, and names the scope (none, targeted, full). (Must pass: no)
requirements.source: TRD Objectives table O5; investigation O5 (issue #154)

requirements.statement: A must-pass criterion proven by a named CI job is re-proved by re-running that job (or the run's failed jobs), never by dispatching the whole workflow; a job also red on the base branch head is reported as baseline, not as a failure of this feature. (Must pass: no)
requirements.source: TRD Objectives table O6; investigation O6 (issue #155)

requirements.statement: The TRD authoring contract does not let a TRD declare a criterion whose only proof is a full manual CI run; the commands that handle a voided, missing or red declared proof name the single-job re-run. (Must pass: no)
requirements.source: TRD Objectives table O7; investigation O7 (issue #155)

requirements.statement: The vendored runtime under .claude/ and the packages/full distribution carry exactly the edited packages/core files (identical content). (Must pass: no)
requirements.source: TRD Objectives table O8; constitution.md Architecture Invariants (Vendored Runtime) and investigation Grounding hazard

requirements.statement: Tests pass with unit coverage at or above 60% and integration coverage at or above 50% where integration tests apply. (Must pass: no)
requirements.source: TRD Objectives table O9; constitution.md Quality Gates

open_questions: OQ-1 | Does a baseline off-host proof settle the criterion, or does it only change the reason? | Assumed: it only changes the reason; the criterion stays not_verifiable, as any non-green proof does (D14). O6 says reported as baseline, not as a failure of this feature, read as reporting, not proving. | Why it matters: settling it met would prove a criterion with a job that never succeeded. | If wrong: a must-pass criterion blocks a feature over a failure that is the base branch's; the fix is to let the blocking policy treat baseline as non-blocking.

OQ-2 | In the regression pass, should a code-class change in a directory no cover shares re-check no-covers criteria? | Assumed: yes; D10 re-checks a no-covers criterion on any code-class change, wider than investigation intended outcome 4 (see NG8). | Why it matters: the source's narrower rule could hide a regression in an uncovered directory. | If wrong: if the owner wants the source's narrowing, D10 gains 'and the file shares a directory with some recorded cover', accepting that risk.

OQ-3 | Should settleOffHost's rule 3 (debugTouchedCovers), which also re-checks no-covers ids on any Debug edit, take the D10 rule? | Assumed: no; out of scope (NG6) because the investigation names only regressionScope. | Why it matters: the two rules now differ for no-covers criteria. | If wrong: a docs-only Debug edit still voids a green off-host proof for a no-covers criterion; a follow-up applies D10 there.

OQ-4 | O4 lists board route among a design criterion's covers. Is the route itself a cover? | Assumed: no; a route is not a repository path. It is the key that finds the page file, which is the cover (D6). | Why it matters: a route string would be dropped as an absolute path by normalizeCoverPath anyway. | If wrong: nothing is lost unless a route file (a router config) is meant to be a cover too; then add the route-list file named in design.md section 3 to each board's covers.

OQ-5 | Which candidate paths does a route-list file line holding the route as a quoted literal yield? | Assumed: its other quoted literals containing / or . (D6). The investigation says to read those lines but not what to take from them. | Why it matters: a router that names a component, not a file, yields nothing and the board is unresolved. | If wrong: more boards stay unresolved than needed; the fix is a resolver for component names in those lines through section 2.

OQ-6 | Where are design maps looked up? | Assumed: every docs/ui/*/design-map.json, refusing a board id found in two (D8, D7). | Why it matters: a product with several designs sharing board ids gets no design covers. | If wrong: read the designs the TRD's Verification Artifacts section names instead.
